svg.title: Voronoi architecture overview
svg.desc: A high-level view of Voronoi. A scientific question is admitted into three nested loops with disjoint authority: an always-on deterministic control loop, an episodic reasoning session inside it, and disposable one-shot workers inside that. All three loops communicate only by reading and appending to a durable evidence substrate of git, Beads and .swarm state. Evidence is submitted to a column of science gates — rigor ladder, validity audit, judgment tribunal, convergence gate and human gate — which either block and force a re-run, or release an evidence-backed result.
svg.text: VORONOI · NESTED AUTONOMY OVER A DURABLE EVIDENCE SUBSTRATE
Three loops of decreasing lifetime and disjoint authority, coupled only through files, released only by a progressive standard of proof.
admits work · collects events · wakes and parks sessions · integrates results · recovers after any crash — and makes no scientific judgment
OBSERVE → ORIENT → DECIDE → ACT, then exit — the session is disposable, its decisions are not
INNER LOOP — EXECUTE → TEST (≤3) → SELF-REVIEW + EVA → COMMIT → EMIT EVENT
19 role definitions · a worker sees only its own task and the substrate
rigor is enforced by code, not by good intentions
the standard of proof is fixed at intake, then escalates
no experiment counts until EVA declares it valid
a surprising result must be explained, not just reported
nothing leaves the system without clearing every gate
the filesystem is the only interface between layers — durable, inspectable, and it survives every crash

g.text: one isolated tree per worker · commits are the unit of work
a versioned task graph with real dependencies
artifacts, content hashes and the run manifest

svg.text: Every layer reads and appends here. No layer trusts another layer’s memory — there is no message bus, no shared RAM and no custom IPC.
Authority is strictly partitioned: the control loop never reasons, the reasoning loop never executes, and workers never coordinate. Every hand-off is a durable write.
